request.content: You are a helpful assistant that translates programming worked examples into other natural languages, maintaining both technical accuracy and the original code formatting.

[[WORKED-EXAMPLE]] [[PROGRAM-NAME]] Pythagorean Theorem (Case 1) [[PROGRAM-DESCRIPTION]] Construct a program that accepts two input values from the user, one for each side of a right-angle triangle. The program uses the Pythagorean theorem (c^2 = a^2 + b^2) to calculate the length of the triangle's hypotenuse. To read the input value from the user, we need to use the input() function. This statement prompts the user to enter the length of side A, then reads the text entered by the user and places it in the variable text. The value that will be stored in variable text is a string. [[LINE03.EXPL1]] We need to convert the input text to its float representation because side A could have a decimal point. For this purpose, we use the conversion function float(). [[LINE03.EXPL2]] Note that this can only be done if user input could be translated into a valid floating-point value. [[LINE04.EXPL1]] We need to read and process the input value that the user enters. To read the input value from the user, we need to use the input() function. This statement prompts the user to enter the length of side B, then reads the text entered by the user and places it in the variable text. The value that will be stored in variable text is a string. [[LINE05.EXPL1]] We need to convert the input text to its float representation because side B could have a decimal point. For this purpose, we use the conversion function float(). [[LINE05.EXPL2]] Note that this can only be done if user input could be translated into a valid floating-point value. [[LINE07.EXPL1]] To compute the length of the triangle's hypotenuse, we need to first compute the square of side A. We square side A by using the exponent operator **. [[LINE07.EXPL2]] Note that side_A ** 2 raises the value of side_A to the power of 2. [[LINE09.EXPL1]] To compute the length of the triangle's hypotenuse, we need to compute the square of side B too. We square side B by using the exponent operator **. [[LINE09.EXPL2]] Note that side_B ** 2 raises the value of side_B to the power of 2. [[LINE11.EXPL1]] We use the Pythagorean theorem to obtain the length of the triangle's hypotenuse. To get the triangle's hypotenuse, we take the square root from the sum of square of side A and square of side B. [[LINE11.EXPL2]] Note that we could take square root of a number by raising that number to the power of 0.5. [[LINE13.EXPL1]] This statement prints to the default standard output stream the the length of the triangle's hypotenuse.
The printed text shows the arguments of the print function separated by the default delimiter (i.e., single space character) and followed by the end-of-line character at the end. In the [[SOURCE-CODE]] section, translate ONLY user-defined string-literals and comments; make sure they are ASCII-folded (i.e., remove any accents or non-ASCII characters).
